_comment: Which provider performs which non-deterministic pass. Data, not code:
principle 7 says any of them must be able to do the same logical job, and
that only holds if swapping one is an edit here rather than a patch.
The reviewer is deliberately a different model from the one running the
interview. A model reviewing its own draft agrees with itself.

architect.name: claude
_note: Which model plays the architect in /idp-design. It is here rather than
in the code for the same reason as every other entry: the collision
check compares two pieces of data, not one piece of data against a
string somebody hard-coded. `init --architect <name>` overrides it for
IDE-69 §12: the critic and the architect must be different models. When
they turn out to be the same, that is recorded as a degradation and
shown to the human — it does not stop the run.

_note_alternatives: The alternative pass of /idp-design deliberately reuses this section
with a different schema (schemas/alternatives.schema.json), as IDE-69
§4.3 specifies. It is the same machinery — a second model that did not
write the draft — pointed at a different question, so a second provider
section would be two places to keep one fact.

fallback.name: claude-subagent
_note: Host-supplied, not a command this script can run. A subagent is a
capability of the agent already driving the session; the script cannot
summon one. The host runs it, then hands the JSON over with
the schema is enforced on our side either way.
A deployment that *does* have a runnable second model puts its command
here under `command` and review() will call it. The key is absent
rather than empty on purpose: absent means nobody promised anything.

_absence_is_recorded: No provider means the pass is skipped and provenance says so. A skipped search must never read as a search that found nothing.
